sections.html:
Taylorsville fills 10.85 square miles of the central Salt Lake Valley at roughly 4,295 feet, inside Salt Lake County. Its main roads are Interstate 215, Bangerter Highway and Redwood Road. The ground is a flat plain left by Lake Bonneville, and a ridge called Bennion Hill rises on the east side.

Growth came before cityhood. Population jumped from 17,448 in 1980 to 52,354 in 1990, and a big portion of today's houses were built then. By 2020 there were 60,448 residents in 20,615 households, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 57,484.

For 2020 to 2024 the survey median for an owner-occupied home is $433,800, and owners live in 71.2% of the homes. Monthly owner costs are $1,844 with a mortgage and $546 without. Gross rent is $1,482 at the median and household income $86,413. Treat the median as a survey figure, since condition moves a given house above or below it.

Homes from that era may call for a new roof, sewer line, windows or electrical panel, and many owners would rather not fund those before a sale. Inspectors working for buyers start with exactly those items.

We also hear from owners with a troublesome tenant, an estate shared by several heirs, a house carrying code citations or a move on a deadline. For them a cash offer as is replaces the repair list, the showings and the commission.

The city's own code enforcement office handles zoning and property rules. Usually an issue is settled quickly after the owner is contacted, though an owner who refuses can face legal action to abate the nuisance.

  • Call code enforcement at 801-955-2013 or 801-955-2053, or submit a complaint through the website.
  • Good Landlord Program licenses ended after June 30, 2023, and rental business licenses are being merged into one category.
  • A house sells more easily once open violations are cleared, so ask for a status check before you list.

Landlords selling a rented house should confirm their business license is current and ask the city what a buyer must do to keep renting.

Drivers rely on Interstate 215, Bangerter Highway, Redwood Road and 2700 West. Schools belong to Granite School District, and the Redwood campus of Salt Lake Community College is in town. Redwood Road at 5400 South became a regional shopping hub in the 1980s, with Harmons and Walmart nearby.

The proposed Midvalley Connector bus line would join the Murray Central TRAX and FrontRunner station to the SLCC Redwood campus and West Valley Central. On 4700 South, buses would use center lanes between about Atherton Drive and Redwood Road. It remains in environmental review without an opening date, so call it a plan, and ask the Utah Transit Authority for current status.

Voters approved incorporation in September 1995, and the city began July 1, 1996. A mayor and five council members, elected by district, run it. Police and code enforcement are city departments, while the Unified Fire Authority provides fire service.

sections.h2: Tax dates for a Taylorsville seller
sections.html:
Salt Lake County taxes are payable by November 30. These are the dates that count for a seller or anyone appealing.

DateWhat happens
July 22Valuation notices go out
August 1Appeals to the Board of Equalization open for 45 days
September 15Appeal deadline, or 45 days after the notice if later
November 1Tax notices must be in the mail
November 30Final day to pay with no penalty
December 1Delinquency begins; penalty is the greater of 2.5% or $10
January 31Penalty falls to the greater of 1% or $10 if paid in full
Fourth Thursday of MayUsual date of the final tax sale

A delinquent property can still be redeemed until March 15 of the fifth year after delinquency.
A primary residence is 45% exempt, on up to one acre. At closing the title company splits the current bill, and anything still owed comes out of your proceeds.

A Notice of Valuation that looks high can be contested before the Board of Equalization. Filing opens August 1 and ends September 15, or 45 days after your notice when that is later. Back your claim with sales of similar houses, repair quotes and photos of problems, for instance an aging roof, a failing sewer line or an outdated electrical panel.

Documents persuade more than a general complaint about the bill. Submit them before the deadline and keep copies.

Many sellers here are landlords, and a few steps smooth the way. Check that your business license is current, collect every lease, the rent roll and the deposit amounts, and notify tenants in writing as each lease requires.

An investor who keeps the tenants wants a rent history with no gaps. A buyer moving in cares about when each lease ends. In both cases, handing over this paperwork early produces a cleaner offer.

sections.h2: Selling with open violations or taxes owed
sections.html:
Neither stops a sale. Clearing a code violation is the simplest fix, and the enforcement office can confirm where it stands before you list. Cannot fix it in time? Tell the buyer, and the price will account for the work.

The title company lists overdue taxes as a payoff and pays them from your proceeds when the sale closes. Since delinquent properties stay redeemable for years, learn the exact amount owed before you set a closing date.

1. Tell us where the house is and what shape it is in.
  2. Our written offer comes back to you, and the choice is yours.
  3. When you say yes, the title company searches for ownership problems, back taxes and liens.
  4. Signing day ends with a recorded deed and payment to you.

Since no bank is involved, there is no appraisal to hold things up. At the closing table, have a photo ID, every key, the garage remotes and the contact details of any tenants. If an heir is signing for an estate, bring the papers showing who has authority to sell. Ask the title company how long each stage tends to take, and plan the move around that. The closing statement lists every charge before you sign.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like
sections.html:
Houses in Taylorsville are bought in their present condition, and accepting the offer is always your decision. Describe the house, and for a rental add the lease terms and rent so the number is firm. A title company runs the closing, and the county records the deed.

Ahead of the request, gather your tax notice, any letters from code enforcement and the mortgage payoff amount. A copy of the lease and the deposit amount helps when a tenant lives there.

faqs.q: How many people live in Taylorsville, Utah?
faqs.a: The 2020 census found 60,448 residents. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 57,484, and the city incorporated July 1, 1996.
Granite School District, formed in 1904 when the Salt Lake County Commission combined 22 of 36 local districts.

faqs.q: When are Taylorsville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County wants payment by November 30. From December 1 the balance is delinquent and a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, applies.

faqs.q: How do I report a code violation in Taylorsville?
faqs.a: Phone the city's code enforcement office at 801-955-2013 or 801-955-2053, or send a complaint through its website.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Taylorsville rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Tenants can stay, and the house is bought as is. Send us the lease terms and rent, and the offer will be clear.
